Strange Attractors was a game made in 2006 for a contest promoting one button games, back before touch smartphones got popular and one button games were still pretty rare. At that time the purpose was accessibility: one button games can be played by many paraplegic people who might find games with more complicated input schemes to be impossible.

Strange Attractors won that contest (I believe, can't find mention of it now), and was a finalist at the IGF that year, and the dev went on to make a sequel which I believe was a commercial product at one time. It's free now though. The sequel is a two button game: one button turns gravity on, and the other button turns anti-gravity on. It's bigger and more colorful, so that's what I've linked, but the original game is still available on the same site. I should say that the original is the only one that I've played to completion, so I'm taking it on faith that the sequel is better, but that first game was really fun.

It is interesting these were some of the problems you had with the film. I took a science fiction class at my university and my teacher was a PhD in the subject and had written at least a dozen books. She proposed a series of principles that made a work of SF well done and not so well done. One of these requirements is that any work cannot "Violate the laws they have set down in their own world" So it is like, we accept that you have this robot that essentially reached singularity but we do not accept that he is defeated the way he was because it violated the fact that he is more brilliant than the minds that defeated him.
